name: apple-mcp
description: Apple MCP tools for contacts, notes, messages, mail, reminders, calendar, and maps integration
long_description: Apple MCP gives LLMs access to Apple's native apps including Contacts, Notes, Messages, Mail, Reminders, Calendar, and Maps. This integration allows LLMs to interact with these apps seamlessly, enabling comprehensive automation of daily tasks like managing contacts, creating notes, sending messages, handling emails, setting reminders, managing calendar events, and navigating with Maps.

tools.name: list_reminder_lists
tools.description: List all Apple Reminders lists with their number of open reminders.

tools.name: list_reminders
tools.description: List or search Apple Reminders, sorted by due date (undated last). Filters combine. By default only open (not completed) reminders are returned.

tools.name: create_reminder
tools.description: Create a reminder in Apple Reminders. Uses the default list if none given.

tools.name: update_reminder
tools.description: Change fields of an existing reminder. Only the fields given are changed; pass null for notes or dueDate to clear them.

tools.name: complete_reminder
tools.description: Mark a reminder as completed (or reopen it with completed: false).

tools.name: delete_reminder
tools.description: Permanently delete a reminder. Requires confirm: true; otherwise previews.

tools.name: list_calendars
tools.description: List all Apple Calendar calendars with their account and writability.

tools.name: list_calendar_events
tools.description: List Apple Calendar events in a time range, sorted by start. Defaults to the next 7 days. The range may not exceed 4 years. Recurring events appear once per occurrence.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.description: Create an event in Apple Calendar. A date-only start (YYYY-MM-DD) creates an all-day event; timed events default to 1 hour if no end is given. Uses the default calendar if none is given.

tools.name: update_calendar_event
tools.description: Change fields of an existing event. Only the fields given are changed; pass null for location, notes or url to clear them. For recurring events pass occurrenceStart and choose span.

tools.name: delete_calendar_event
tools.description: Permanently delete a calendar event. Requires confirm: true; otherwise previews. For recurring events pass occurrenceStart and choose span.

tools.name: list_note_folders
tools.description: List all Apple Notes folders with their account and note count.

tools.name: list_notes
tools.description: List Apple Notes, sorted by last modified, newest first. Returns snippets only; use read_note for the full text.

tools.name: read_note
tools.description: Read one Apple Note in full (plain text, optionally raw HTML). Locked (password-protected) notes return no text.

tools.name: create_note
tools.description: Create an Apple Note. With format text the body is converted line by line; the title becomes the note's heading. Uses the default folder if none is given.

tools.name: update_note
tools.description: Change an existing note. title renames it, body REPLACES everything below the title, append adds to the end (body and append are mutually exclusive). Requires confirm: true (otherwise previews) when replacing the body or when the note has attachments or is shared; renaming or appending to a plain note applies directly.

tools.name: delete_note
tools.description: Delete a note (moves it to "Recently Deleted"). Requires confirm: true; otherwise previews.

tools.name: list_message_chats
tools.description: List recent Messages (iMessage/SMS) conversations, newest first: chat id, display name (groups), participant handles, last message date and unread count. Use the chat id with read_messages, search_messages or send_message. Contact names are not resolved: handles are phone numbers or emails.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Read messages of one conversation, newest first. Identify it by chatId (from list_message_chats) or by handle (phone number or email, one-to-one chats only). Optionally restrict to before/after an ISO date.

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Search message text (case-insensitive substring) across all chats or within one chat, newest first. Scans the most recent ~5000 messages.

tools.name: list_unread_messages
tools.description: List unread incoming messages across all chats, newest first.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send an iMessage/SMS via the Messages app to a handle (phone number or email) or an existing chat (chatId, needed for group chats). Provide exactly one of `to` or `chatId`. Requires confirm: true; without it only a preview of the recipient and exact text is returned and nothing is sent.

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.description: Search Apple Contacts by name, organisation, nickname, email or phone number (case-insensitive; all words must match). Returns id, name, organisation, phones and emails; use get_contact for full details.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: Get one contact in full: all phones and emails with labels, postal addresses, organisation, job title, birthday and URLs. The note field is not available.

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description: List contacts sorted by name, one page at a time. Use offset to page through; the summary line shows the total.

tools.name: find_contact_by_phone
tools.description: Find who a phone number belongs to. Matches regardless of formatting and country prefix, so "+49 171 1234567" finds a contact stored as "0171 1234567".

tools.name: create_contact
tools.description: Create a new contact in the default account. Needs at least a name or an organisation. Birthday as YYYY-MM-DD (or --MM-DD).

tools.name: update_contact
tools.description: Change a contact. Adding phones/emails/urls (addPhones, addEmails, addUrls) or filling an empty field applies immediately; changing or clearing a field that already has a value requires confirm: true, otherwise it previews. Pass null to clear a field.

tools.name: search_places
tools.description: Search Apple Maps for places (businesses, stations, addresses, landmarks) and return name, address, coordinates, phone, website and category. Read-only; does not open Maps. Without `near`, results come from the Mac's default region. `near` is best effort: results are merged and sorted by distance to that area, but far-away cities can yield few hits; then search for a specific name instead.

tools.name: get_directions
tools.description: Calculate a route between two places with Apple Maps data: distance, expected travel time and (for driving and walking) turn-by-turn steps, plus alternatives. Read-only; does not open Maps (use open_in_maps for that). Transit returns only an estimate of distance and time. `from` and `to` are place names, addresses or "lat,lon"; include the city to avoid ambiguity.

tools.name: open_in_maps
tools.description: UI SIDE EFFECT: opens and brings the Maps app to the front, showing a place search or a route. Use only when the user wants to see it in Maps; for data use search_places or get_directions. Give `query` for a place, or `to` (optionally `from`, default current location) for a route. Cannot save favorites, guides or pins: Maps offers no API for that.

tools.name: list_email_accounts
tools.description: List the accounts configured in Apple Mail, with their email addresses.

tools.name: list_email_folders
tools.description: List Apple Mail folders (mailboxes) with unread and total message counts, optionally for one account.

tools.name: list_emails
tools.description: List emails in a folder, newest first, with sender, date, read/flagged state and a short snippet. Defaults to the INBOX of all accounts. Use read_email for the full text and search_emails to look for something.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.description: Search emails, newest first. Each word of query must appear (case-insensitive) in the subject, sender name/address or the message preview text; full bodies are not searched. Searches the INBOX unless a folder is given. Optional date range.

tools.name: read_email
tools.description: Read one email in full: plain-text body, recipients (to/cc) and attachment names.

tools.name: create_draft
tools.description: Save a new email as a draft in Apple Mail's Drafts folder without sending it and without opening a compose window. No confirmation needed. It lands in the Drafts folder of the sending account and can take a minute to show up in list_emails / search_emails (Mail indexes it after syncing).

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send a new email. Requires confirm: true; without it only a preview of from/to/cc/bcc/subject/body is returned and nothing is sent.

tools.name: reply_email
tools.description: Reply to an email. By default only saves a reply DRAFT (quoting the original) that the user can review in Mail. With send: true the reply is sent, which requires confirm: true (otherwise a preview is returned).

tools.name: move_email
tools.description: Move an email to another folder of its account (use list_email_folders for names; "Account/Folder" targets another account). The id stays valid. Moving to Trash/Deleted/Junk/Spam requires confirm: true (otherwise previews); other moves apply directly.

tools.name: mark_email_read
tools.description: Mark an email as read (default) or unread.

tools.name: flag_email
tools.description: Flag (default) or unflag an email.

tools.name: read_pdf
tools.description: Extract the text of a PDF file, page by page, with '--- Page N ---' markers and the total page count. Use fromPage/toPage (1-based) to read a range. Output is capped at maxChars; if truncated, the result says which page to continue from. Locked PDFs return an error; scanned PDFs without a text layer are reported explicitly (OCR is not supported). Use get_pdf_info for metadata only.

tools.name: get_pdf_info
tools.description: Get PDF metadata without reading the full text: page count, title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer, creation/modification dates, encrypted flag, file size, and whether the PDF has a text layer (sampled from a few pages; false suggests a scanned document).

tools.name: search_pdf
tools.description: Case-insensitive plain-text search inside one PDF. Returns page numbers with short context snippets (one entry per occurrence), up to `limit`. Use read_pdf with a page range to read the surrounding text.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files and folders in a directory (default: home). Returns path, name, type (file/dir/symlink), size in bytes and modified time; folders first, then by name. Use depth 1-5 to recurse and `pattern` (e.g. '*.pdf', 'report*') to filter by name. For content/metadata search across the Mac use the Finder search tool.

tools.name: get_file_info
tools.description: Get metadata for a file or folder: type, kind, size, created/modified dates, permissions and symlink target (shown only if the target is an allowed location).

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file (lines offset/limit, output capped at ~100 KB). Also extracts plain text from .docx .doc .rtf .rtfd .odt .html .webarchive. Binary files are refused; use read_pdf for PDFs. If truncated, call again with a higher offset.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write text to a file. mode 'create' (default) fails if the file exists; 'append' adds to the end; 'overwrite' replaces an existing file and needs confirm: true (without it you get a preview). Parent folders are created only with createDirs: true. Overwrites are atomic.

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Create a folder (and missing parents). No-op if it already exists.

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Move or rename a file or folder. If the destination already exists it would be replaced, which needs confirm: true (preview first). Destination is the full new path, not a folder to move into.

tools.name: trash_file
tools.description: Move a file or folder to the Trash (recoverable from Finder). Always requires confirm: true; without it you get a preview. Nothing is ever permanently deleted.

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search files and folders with macOS Spotlight. 'query' matches file names and file contents (all words must match); set nameOnly to match names only. '*' in the query is literal unless wildcards is true. Filter by kind, modified date range and folder. Results (path, name, kind, size, modified) are sorted newest-modified first and limited to allowed folders. Only indexed locations are searched. For listing the contents of one folder use the files tools instead.

tools.name: list_recent_files
tools.description: List files and folders the user opened or used recently (Spotlight last-used date), newest-modified first. Defaults to the last 7 days.

tools.name: get_finder_selection
tools.description: Read-only: the paths currently selected in the frontmost Finder window, plus the folder that window shows. Empty when nothing is selected or no window is open. Paths outside the allowed folders are left out.

tools.name: reveal_in_finder
tools.description: UI side effect: opens a Finder window showing the file or folder, selects it and brings Finder to the front. Use only when the user wants to see it in Finder.

tools.name: get_file_tags
tools.description: Read the Finder tags (e.g. 'Red', 'Work') of a file or folder.

tools.name: set_file_tags
tools.description: Change the Finder tags of a file or folder. mode 'add' (default) adds tags and needs no confirmation; 'remove' removes the given tags and 'replace' sets exactly the given tags (empty list clears all) -- both require confirm: true when they would drop existing tags (otherwise they preview).

tools.name: list_shortcuts
tools.description: List the user's Apple Shortcuts (name, identifier, folder). Optional filters: 'folder' (folder name or identifier; 'none' for shortcuts not in a folder) and 'query' (case-insensitive name substring). Set includeFolders to also return the folder list. Use this to find the exact name/identifier before run_shortcut. Results are cached for about 30 seconds.

tools.name: run_shortcut
tools.description: Run an Apple Shortcut by name or identifier, optionally with text input ('input') or a file as input ('inputPath'), and capture its output (text is returned inline; other output types are saved to a temp file whose path and type are returned). A shortcut can do anything the user's Shortcuts can (send messages, change files, control devices), so this ALWAYS requires confirm: true: call first without it to get a preview naming the exact shortcut and input, show that to the user, then call again with confirm: true. Exception: shortcuts whose name or identifier is listed in the server's APPLE_MCP_SHORTCUTS_ALLOW environment variable (comma-separated, case-insensitive) run without confirmation. Unknown or ambiguous names return an error with close matches; use list_shortcuts. timeoutSeconds defaults to 60 (max 300); shortcuts that wait for UI interaction will time out.

tools.name: view_shortcut
tools.description: Open a shortcut in the Shortcuts app editor (UI side effect: launches/foregrounds Shortcuts and shows the shortcut; it does not run it). Accepts a name or identifier; ambiguous names return an error listing identifiers.

tools.name: music_now_playing
tools.description: Apple Music player state: current track (name, artist, album, duration and position in seconds), volume 0-100, shuffle and repeat. Does not launch Music; returns "Music is not running" if it is closed.

tools.name: music_play
tools.description: This affects audio playback on the Mac. Starts audio in Apple Music (launches Music if needed). With no arguments it resumes playback. To play something specific give an id (track or playlist persistent id from music_search_library / music_list_playlists) or an exact name plus optional kind (track, playlist, album, artist) and artist. Ambiguous matches return an error listing candidates; retry with an id or more detail. Albums/artists start at the first matching track.

tools.name: music_pause
tools.description: This affects audio playback on the Mac. Pauses Apple Music playback. Fails if Music is not running.

tools.name: music_next_track
tools.description: This affects audio playback on the Mac. Skips to the next track in Apple Music.

tools.name: music_previous_track
tools.description: This affects audio playback on the Mac. Goes to the previous track (or the start of the current one) in Apple Music.

tools.name: music_set_volume
tools.description: This affects audio playback on the Mac. Sets the Music app volume: level is absolute 0-100, delta is relative (e.g. -10, +15); give exactly one. The result is clamped to 0-100.

tools.name: music_search_library
tools.description: Search the LOCAL Apple Music library (not the streaming catalog) by text in name, artist or album. kind track returns songs with persistent ids (use them for music_play / music_add_to_playlist); album and artist return grouped names with track counts.

tools.name: music_list_playlists
tools.description: List Apple Music user playlists with id and track count. Smart playlists, folders and system playlists are skipped unless includeAll is true.

tools.name: music_add_to_playlist
tools.description: Add library tracks (by persistent id) to an existing user playlist. Additive, no confirmation needed. Smart, folder and system playlists cannot be targeted.

tools.name: music_create_playlist
tools.description: Create a new empty user playlist in Apple Music, optionally with initial tracks. No confirmation needed.

tools.name: music_remove_from_playlist
tools.description: Remove tracks from a user playlist (the tracks stay in the library). Requires confirm: true; otherwise returns a preview of what would be removed.

tools.name: obsidian_list_vaults
tools.description: List the Obsidian vaults on this Mac: name (folder name), path, number of notes, when last opened and whether it is currently open in Obsidian. Start here to get the vault name the other obsidian_* tools take.

tools.name: obsidian_list_notes
tools.description: List Markdown notes in an Obsidian vault (optionally one folder), newest-modified first. Returns vault-relative path, title, modified time and size. Skips .obsidian, .trash and other dot-folders. Use obsidian_search_notes to find by content.

tools.name: obsidian_search_notes
tools.description: Search an Obsidian vault by file name and content (case-insensitive; every word must appear). Optional tag filter (#tag in the body or tags: in frontmatter; parent tags match nested ones) and folder. Returns vault-relative path, title, modified time and 1-2 context snippets. Name matches rank first, then newest. Files over 1 MB are matched by name only.

tools.name: obsidian_read_note
tools.description: Read one Obsidian note by vault-relative path ('Projects/Plan.md') or by note name as in a [[wikilink]] ('Plan'; an ambiguous name returns the candidate paths). Returns parsed frontmatter (scalars and lists), the body (paged with offset/limit in characters), outgoing [[links]]/embeds and tags. includeBacklinks scans the vault for notes linking here (capped at 50).

tools.name: obsidian_write_note
tools.description: Create or modify a Markdown note in an Obsidian vault. mode 'create' (default) fails if the note exists; 'append' adds content at the end and 'prepend' right after the frontmatter (both need an existing note, no confirmation); 'overwrite' replaces the whole note and, if it exists, requires confirm: true (preview first). Folders are created as needed. The path is vault-relative; '.md' is added if missing. Writes inside .obsidian or other dot-folders are refused.

tools.name: obsidian_daily_note
tools.description: Read or append to the daily note of an Obsidian vault (today by default, or a date given as YYYY-MM-DD). Honors the vault's daily-notes settings (folder, date format, simple template). 'append' adds text at the end and creates the note (from the template, if any) when it does not exist yet; no confirmation needed.

tools.name: obsidian_open_note
tools.description: Open a vault, or a note in it, in the Obsidian app (obsidian:// URL). Brings Obsidian to the front: only use when the user wants to see the note. To read content use obsidian_read_note.
